hero.name: Ahmed Hany Khairy
hero.role_qualifier: Data Engineering Trainee @ DEPI · AI Engineering Student
hero.positioning_statement: I build ETL pipelines with Python and SQL — from raw multi-source files to validated, well-modeled PostgreSQL warehouses — currently training in the DEPI Data Engineering track while finishing my BSc in Artificial Intelligence.
hero.diagram: Visual pipeline/lineage connecting the portrait to the data systems he works with (source files, transformation, PostgreSQL warehouse); accessible text equivalent required.

about.human_paragraph: I'm Ahmed — an Artificial Intelligence undergraduate at the Faculty of Artificial Intelligence in Kafr El-Sheikh, based in Cairo. Outside coursework you'll find me in programming-club workshops and algorithmic problem-solving sessions, or building database-automation tools with teammates at hackathons.
about.engineering_paragraph: My work sits on the path from raw files to reliable data: extraction scripts that ingest multi-source batches, transformation routines with type casting, null checks and duplicate removal, and normalized PostgreSQL warehouses queried through tuned SQL. I like the parts of the job where correctness is measurable.

flow_diagram.text_equivalent: Ahmed's work follows the data path: raw multi-source files are extracted, transformed with validated Python and SQL routines, loaded into a normalized PostgreSQL warehouse, and queried through optimized SQL.

projects.title: Smartphone Specification Analysis 2025
projects.one_liner: Exploratory analysis of 930+ smartphones across the 2025 market — comparing specifications, pricing, and performance tiers.
projects.purpose: Examine trends in the 2025 smartphone market by comparing device specifications, pricing, and performance tiers across multiple brands.
highlights: Data cleaning and preprocessing: missing-value handling, duplicate detection and removal, outlier analysis and filtering
Feature engineering: categorization into RAM-based performance tiers — Budget, Mid-Range, Flagship
Statistical analysis and feature normalization for unbiased comparison across specifications and pricing
Visual analysis: pricing vs. performance scatter plots, specification distribution histograms (RAM, battery, display), and market trend analysis

pipeline.text_equivalent: The notebook loads the smartphone dataset, cleans it (missing values, duplicates, outliers), engineers RAM-based performance tiers, runs descriptive statistics on normalized features, and produces comparison visualizations.

preview.alt: Jupyter Notebook screenshot of the smartphone analysis: dataset preview, performance-versus-price scatter plot, and weight distribution histogram

projects.results: Analysis outputs only — statistics, tier comparisons, and visualizations. No deployment, live demo, or production claims.

projects.title: DataFlow Monitor
projects.one_liner: A monitoring dashboard that tracks ETL/ELT pipelines in real time — pipeline health, throughput, quality metrics, and alerts across multiple data sources.
projects.purpose: Track ETL/ELT data pipelines in real time: visualize pipeline health, data throughput, quality metrics, and alerts across multiple data sources.
highlights: Real-time pipeline status tracking: active job monitoring, automated stage completion logging, instant failure and bottleneck alerts
Data-flow architecture visualization: data movement and transformation paths, dynamic component connection diagrams
Throughput and latency monitoring: processing rates, payload metrics, and bottleneck tracking
Data quality scoring: completeness and freshness evaluation

pipeline.text_equivalent: Data from sources such as APIs, Kafka streams, and FTP feeds is extracted, transformed, and loaded into a warehouse or analytics database, while the dashboard tracks health, throughput, latency, and data quality at every stage.

preview.alt: DataFlow Monitor dashboard showing the pipeline flow architecture, pipeline performance bars, 24-hour throughput chart, and data quality alerts

projects.results: Built application interface; no deployment or live demo documented.

projects.title: BusinessInsights Hub
projects.one_liner: A BI platform that consolidates sales, customer, inventory, and finance data into one interactive dashboard for KPI tracking and data-driven decisions.
projects.purpose: Consolidate data from multiple sources — sales, customers, inventory, finance — into a single interactive interface that helps businesses track KPIs, analyze revenue trends, segment customers, and make data-driven decisions.
highlights: Unified KPI and revenue analytics: real-time tracking for revenue, profit margins, and active customers; monthly/yearly trend comparisons; category-wise sales breakdowns
Customer segmentation: automated RFM (Recency, Frequency, Monetary) classification, behavioral tracking across sales channels, retention and churn-risk metrics
Inventory and product performance: top-product rankings by sales volume and margin, low-stock and reorder-point notifications, stock turn rate analysis
Interactive reporting: dynamic date-range and multi-region filtering, scheduled PDF/Excel exports, low-latency dashboard caching with Redis

pipeline.text_equivalent: Sales, customer, inventory, and finance data is moved through an Airflow pipeline with dbt transformations and Spark processing, stored in PostgreSQL with Redis caching, and served through a Next.js analytics dashboard with exportable reports.

preview.alt: BusinessInsights Hub dashboard with KPI cards, monthly revenue trend, sales by category, top products ranking, and customer segmentation scatter plot

projects.results: Built application interface; no deployment or live demo documented.

optional_pipeline_replay.recommendation: All three project documents describe enough architecture for a static architecture walkthrough per project. An interactive sample-data replay is most defensible for DataFlow Monitor; if built later it must carry the label 'Interactive demonstration using sample data'. Final call belongs to the case-study phase.
